children: The U.S. labor market is likely to remain resilient enough to support further Federal Reserve rate hikes, with BNP Paribas forecasting a 90K increase in September nonfarm payrolls and a 4.0% unemployment rate.

The forecast would put September job growth well above BNP Paribas' estimated negative 20K breakeven rate for the second half of 2026. The bank said economic momentum should keep the jobless rate moving lower into early 2027.

BNP Paribas expected private-sector employment to rise by 90K in September, with government payrolls unchanged. It forecasts continued momentum in construction and manufacturing, particularly in nonresidential construction tied to the data-center buildout, while expecting a more typical 10K gain in leisure and hospitality.

The bank projected unemployment at 4.03%, down from 4.14% in August, partly reflecting an expected 0.1 percentage-point decline in labor-force participation. It also forecasts average hourly earnings to rise 0.3% month over month, equivalent to 3.2% year over year, up from 3.1% in August.

BNP Paribas said recent company surveys pointed to stronger labor demand and rising wage pressures. Its Q3 CFO survey showed average wages expected to rise 4.3% in both 2026 and 2027, up from estimates of 4.0% and 3.9%, respectively, in the prior-quarter survey.

The bank also raised its estimate for third-quarter GDP growth to a 3.7% annualized pace from 2.7% previously, citing stronger consumer growth. It pointed to increased labor demand, higher hiring plans and vacancies, and positive economic effects from AI investment and equity-market wealth.

BNP Paribas said the projected cumulative 75 basis points of Fed tightening in its base case should be viewed as a floor, with risks tilted toward more rate increases. It also said a steeper-than-expected decline in unemployment could bring wage growth back into the Fed's focus as an inflationary driver.

title: BNP Paribas sees September jobs report supporting further Fed hikes
